slides.texte_overlay: Don't skip breakfast before hard thinking. A real breakfast with eggs, oats or yogurt keeps your focus steady through the morning.
Eat more fatty fish. Salmon, sardines, mackerel. Two portions a week bring omega-3 fats that your brain uses every single day.
Keep snacks simple. A handful of nuts, an apple, some dark chocolate. Better snacks mean fewer afternoon crashes and a much clearer head.
Eat colourful vegetables at every meal. Greens, peppers, carrots, beetroot. Different colours bring different nutrients your body and brain need.
Before: I fed my body well but my mind only got scrolling. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and my brain feels fed too.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: I fed my body well but my mind only got scrolling. After: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. My brain feels fed too.

slides.texte_overlay: Don't eat a huge lunch before important work. A lighter lunch keeps you sharp and awake. A heavy one makes your afternoon slow and foggy.
Stop eating two or three hours before bed. Your sleep gets deeper, and deep sleep is when your brain sorts and stores everything you learned.
